item.title: NFL Insiders Reveal What Detroit Lions Are Seeking Before Trade Deadline
item.description: The Detroit Lions are running out of time to make a move before the 2026 NFL trade deadline, and multiple national insiders believe general manager Brad Holmes is looking for help on defense. With Tuesday’s deadline rapidly approaching, Detroit has emerged as a team worth monitoring. The biggest priority appears to be cornerback, a position that has generated plenty of discussion throughout the season. But that might not be the only area Holmes is evaluating as the Lions prepare for the second half of their schedule. According to reporting from ESPN’s Dan Graziano, Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer, and The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones, the Lions have been exploring opportunities to strengthen their secondary. Linebacker is another potential area of interest following the frightening injury to Jack Campbell. And with the trade deadline set for Tuesday, November 10, at 4 p.m. ET , Holmes has a limited window to improve a roster that is now 6-2 following Sunday’s 19-9 victory over the Miami Dolphins. The question is whether Detroit will find the right opportunity to make a meaningful upgrade. Detroit Lions general manager Brad Holmes takes a selfie with fans at warmup ahead of the game between Arizona Cardinals and Detroit Lions at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Arizona on Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Multiple NFL Insiders Point to Detroit’s Biggest Need The Lions’ search for cornerback help has become one of the more consistent storylines surrounding this year’s trade deadline. Several national reporters have identified Detroit as a team that could be active in the market for another defensive back. In his November 4 reporting, ESPN insider Dan Graziano revealed that both Detroit and the Chicago Bears have been checking on potentially available cornerbacks. That report provided another indication that Holmes is evaluating his options rather than simply standing pat with his current roster. Meanwhile, Breer offered a similar assessment while discussing Detroit’s situation. He indicated that the Lions have been looking around the league for potential help in the secondary. “I would say right now they are looking for secondary help and they have been looking around for corners,” Breer explained, as documented in a November 3 Lions Wire report . More recently, Jones added another intriguing possibility to the conversation. In his November 7 reporting, Jones indicated that Detroit and Chicago would both like to add cornerback help at the right price. Jones also suggested Denver as a team that could attract interest because of its depth at the position. That doesn’t mean Detroit has entered negotiations with the Broncos, but it provides another potential direction for Holmes as the deadline approaches. item.title: Incident-by-incident: Was it a bad weekend for VAR?
item.description: Manchester United's last-gasp equaliser against Aston Villa survived a VAR review for a potential foul [Getty Images] Whisper it quietly, but the statistics say video assistant referee decisions have been pretty good in the Premier League so far this season. The Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel, which looks at every contentious decision and votes whether it is right or wrong, reported just two VAR errors after eight rounds of matches. At the same stage last season, there had been six mistakes. Then came this weekend, during which almost every top-flight game had a controversial decision. BBC Sport looks at most of these situations - there really were too many to do them all - and assesses the likelihood that the KMI Panel will add to the list of errors. Manchester United 4-4 Aston Villa Incident 1: Penalty awarded to Manchester United for a foul by Boubacar Kamara on Matheus Cunha in the 16th minute. Verdict: The spot-kick was awarded because the Villa defender went through Cunha to win the ball. Replays clearly showed the first contact was on the Brazilian's foot. What the KMI Panel might say: This will be a correct decision. Incident 2: Possible foul by Senne Lammens on Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki before Patrick Dorgu's 96th-minute equaliser. Verdict : There are similarities to a goal Arsenal scored at Old Trafford last season, when William Saliba leant into United goalkeeper Altay Bayındır. Lammens was not looking at the ball, which increases the chances of a VAR intervention. What the KMI Panel might say: With the higher bar for an intervention in the Premier League, and minimal contact, it is unlikely to be a VAR error not to disallow the goal. Arsenal 1-0 Hull Incident: Kai Havertz was pulled down inside the area by Nobel Mendy. The VAR, Michael Oliver, sent referee Farai Hallam to the pitchside monitor for a penalty, but it was not given due to an offside offence by the Germany international. Verdict: BBC Sport covered this incident in detail on Saturday . As the foul happened before any potential offside offence, the penalty should have been awarded. What the KMI Panel might say: Even though it feels wrong to reward a player in an offside position with a penalty, the law says otherwise and this is likely to be a mistake. Leeds 1-0 Tottenham Incident: Omar Bogle fouled Mathys Tel, with referee John Brooks giving the free-kick but no sanction for the Leeds player. The VAR, Tony Harrington, opted not to send Brooks to the monitor for a red card. Verdict: BBC Sport covered the merits of this incident on Saturday . It was a difficult call for the VAR, because Bogle caused the foul with his supporting rather than his challenging foot. Still, it was a very painful challenge and some believe it should have been a red card. What the KMI Panel might say: Was it an unfortunate incident, or a tackle which endangered the opponent? item.title: Kettering Town 'can not hide' from its racism problem
item.description: Kettering Town's director of football said the club could no longer hide behind "the comforting lie" that the abuse came from "a small minority" [Getty Images] Non-league Kettering Town have said they "can no longer hide" from the issue of racism after a visiting player was allegedly subjected to "sickening" abuse. Redditch United player Dan Sweeney said he was targeted by a Kettering supporter during Saturday's Southern League Premier Division Central tie at the Poppies' Latimer Park stadium, which the hosts won 2-1. The incident comes after a match official reported alleged racial abuse at a Kettering fixture last season , and a previous instance of alleged racist abuse against a Redditch player at Latimer Park in 2017 . In a statement, Kettering director of football Fabian Forde said the "poison" of racism went beyond matchdays. He also spoke out against the presence of what he called "festering" racism on the club's fans forums. Writing on the club's website , Forde said: "Let's be completely honest with ourselves: this is not the first time. We can no longer hide behind the comforting lie that 'it's just a small minority' or 'they don't reflect the majority of our fans'. "Every single time we dismiss hate by calling it a minority issue, we minimise the damage. The truth is, if the majority stays silent, that small minority becomes our identity. "They tarnish our reputation in the eyes of opposition players, fans, and officials. They make our club look like a haven for bigotry. Is that really who we want to be?" Forde added that the club could not "keep sending out generic statements that mean nothing" and urged fans to support "real cultural change" by taking responsibility for calling out the perpetrators of racist abuse. He said: "To the majority of our fans, the good, decent people who love this club for the right reasons, we are pleading with you. "We need you to stand up. We need you to confront this minority head-on. If you see someone typing hate online, call them out. If you hear someone shouting abuse next to you on a Saturday afternoon, don't look away. "Tell a steward. Identify them to the club. Why are we protecting people who are actively destroying the reputation of the club we love?" Northamptonshire Police said Saturday's alleged incident had not yet been reported to officers [Getty Images] In relation to Saturday's incident, Northamptonshire Police said they had "not identified any report relating to this allegation." However, the force said: "It may be that any report is awaiting allocation or has been made to another police force. item.title: Titans WR had 'incident' involving law enforcement at Nashville airport
item.description: The bye week was not all quiet for the Tennessee Titans . Wide receiver Calvin Ridley was involved in an incident at Nashville International Airport over the weekend, with details remaining scant other than the Titans acknowledging they are aware of the "incident" and are communicating with the Metro Nashville Airport Authority. "With regards to Calvin, we’re aware of everything that’s happening. From my understanding, it was a very minor miscommunication at the airport," Titans head coach Robert Saleh said Monday, Nov. 9. "Unfortunately, the law enforcement (agencies) have it, and that’s about as far as I can go with commenting." Ridley has six catches for 91 yards in seven games this season and could be a candidate to be moved to another team prior to Tuesday's trade deadline. The Titans are coming off their extended rest with a 1-7 record and heading into a Nov. 15 matchup against the AFC South's first-place Jacksonville Jaguars . It has not been a smooth season for Tennessee. The Titans released defensive lineman Jordan Elliott last month after he pulled a gun and threatened a teammate in the parking lot of the team's facility. Saleh was asked if the latest Ridley development was "frustrating," but the former head coach of the New York Jets would not go that far. “I think when you’re losing everything’s exacerbated, but all thirty-two teams deal with things throughout the season," Saleh said. "But yeah, it’s unfortunate with what happened.” A first-round pick of the Atlanta Falcons in 2018, Ridley has also played for the Jacksonville Jaguars and Tennessee Titans. He served a suspension during the 2022 season for betting on NFL games while he was injured the previous season. This is his third season of a four-year, $92 million contract he signed with Tennessee. item.description: Journalist claims Liverpool star is set to leave with Premier League replacement considered Alisson likely to depart as Lynch reveals previous Liverpool interest in Premier League keeper David Lynch expects Alisson Becker to leave Liverpool at the end of the season and has identified Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen as a player the club have previously tracked. Speaking on Anfield Index’s Media Matters podcast, Lynch praised Alisson’s performance against Crystal Palace but suggested that one outstanding display would not determine Liverpool’s longer-term decision. His comments point towards a potentially significant summer in the goalkeeping department. However, he did not report an agreed Alisson departure or confirm that Liverpool are currently negotiating for Verbruggen. Alisson brilliance does not change Lynch’s expectation Alisson was central to Liverpool’s victory at Palace, producing the kind of saves that have defined his Anfield career. Lynch described the performance as “absolutely back to his best”, while arguing that Liverpool must consider a broader picture when assessing another contract. “I don’t think this is going to convince Liverpool to give him a new contract,” he said. “I think we’re moving towards a situation where he leaves at the end of the season, but he’s got a lot of matches to contribute to before then.” That distinction matters. Lynch believes Alisson can still decide important games while also expecting the club to move towards a different long-term arrangement. The Palace performance demonstrated his continuing ability. It did not, in Lynch’s view, remove concerns about availability or consistency across an entire campaign. Contract and injury history shape assessment Discussing the likelihood of an extension, Lynch was emphatic. “I’d be quite frankly amazed if he stays because he’s out of contract at the end of the season,” he said. He cited Alisson’s injury history and what he considers a decline from the extraordinary standards established earlier in his Liverpool career. “He was fantastic yesterday, but in general we’re seeing a decline in performances from that absolutely incredible level that he used to be at,” Lynch added. “I would expect him to depart at the end of the season. Absolutely.” Those remarks represent Lynch’s expectation rather than an announcement from Liverpool or the goalkeeper. No destination was established during the discussion. They nevertheless underline the difficult judgement involved: how much weight Liverpool should place on a player’s highest level compared with the frequency with which he can deliver it. Verbruggen interest predates Brighton move Asked about potential alternatives, Lynch offered one specific piece of information about Verbruggen. “What I can say with confidence is I know for a fact that Liverpool were tracking him prior to his move to Brighton,” he said. item.title: Report: Bills have scanned safety pool before NFL trade deadline
item.description: In the aftermath of the Jaguars monster trade to acquire Falcons safety Jessie Bates, a report has surfaced about the Buffalo Bills and their interest in that same position. Here’s what ESPN NFL Insider Jeremy Fowler tweet on the subject: Jaguars swung big at safety but aren't only ones in that market. Bills have scanned the safety pool of late. My sense is Budda Baker would welcome chance to play for contender if AZ entertains talks (big if). Tennessee has calls on Amani Hooker but wants to keep him. — Jeremy Fowler (@JFowlerESPN) November 9, 2026 While the Bills have plenty of bodies — and upside — at safety, after the release of C.J. Gardner-Johnson they certainly could use a veteran upgrade at the position. We did feature Baker in our trade-deadline candidate here at Rumblings, and it’s not exactly my favorite idea. Why? Because he’s a rather expensive, box defender – free safety hybrid who’s established his quality reputation mostly on tenacity as a tackler… not as a ball hawk. I’m of the belief they need better, more dynamic coverage players at the safety spot. And this is the second-consecutive season Baker has taken a clear step backward in coverage. Now, when Gardner-Johnson was let go, he was carrying the worst missed tackle rate among qualifying safeties in the NFL. Baker is much more reliable in that regard, Jim Leonhard made no mistake about his tackling emphasis this offseason. Let’s see if the Bills’ swing is for the 30-year-old Baker, who averages 90 tackles, six pass breakups, and one pick per season, or if Buffalo goes in a different direction at safety (or another position). *there are two coaching connections to Baker, as Bills WR coach Drew Terrell and special teams coordinator Jeff Rodgers were both in Arizona with the safety for multiple seasons.

item.title: Today in Motorsport History, November 9: Rosberg Won the 2014 Brazilian Grand Prix as Hamilton’s Spin Kept the Title Fight Alive
item.description: Nico Rosberg in the Mercedes F1 W05 Hybrid at Suzuka during the 2014 Japanese Grand Prix. Illustrative image, not from the Brazilian Grand Prix. Photo: Takayuki Suzuki / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0) Nico Rosberg won the 2014 Brazilian Grand Prix at Interlagos on November 9, 2014, beating Mercedes teammate Lewis Hamilton by 1.457 seconds. Hamilton’s spin on lap 28 decided the race, and the result trimmed his championship lead to 17 points with one round left, a finale that was going to pay double points. What happened at the 2014 Brazilian Grand Prix Rosberg took pole position with a 1:10.023 and led the early laps of the 71-lap race. He pitted from the lead on lap 7 and Hamilton followed a lap later, which let Nico Hülkenberg, on a different strategy, lead for a handful of laps. Rosberg passed Hülkenberg for the lead on lap 14, and Hamilton did the same a lap after that, setting up a two-car Mercedes fight. The swing came after the second round of stops. Rosberg pitted on lap 26 and handed Hamilton the lead, but Hamilton’s tyres were finished. On lap 28 he locked his rear tyres under braking, spun onto the run-off area, and rejoined 7.4 seconds behind Rosberg. Rosberg made his last stop around lap 50, stayed in front, and held off Hamilton over the final laps. Hamilton set the fastest lap, a 1:13.555 on lap 62, and still finished 1.457 seconds adrift. Formula 1’s own race analysis described it as a dominant Rosberg performance that set up the title decider. Lewis Hamilton in the Mercedes F1 W05 Hybrid at Suzuka during the 2014 Japanese Grand Prix. Illustrative image, not from the Brazilian Grand Prix. Photo: Takayuki Suzuki / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0) Felipe Massa completed the podium for Williams, 41.031 seconds back, even after a five-second penalty for speeding in the pit lane. Jenson Button was fourth, Sebastian Vettel fifth and Fernando Alonso sixth. The one-two was Mercedes’ 11th of the season, a Formula 1 record at the time. The competitive context: a title fight with a strange rulebook Hamilton arrived in São Paulo 24 points clear of Rosberg, 316 to 292. Brazil could not settle anything, because the Abu Dhabi finale was set to award double points. Even if Hamilton had won and Rosberg had scored nothing, Rosberg would still have been 49 points back and mathematically alive. Rosberg’s win, worth 25 points to Hamilton’s 18, moved the totals to 334 and 317. That left Rosberg needing to win the finale and have Hamilton finish third or lower. Anything else, and the champion was Hamilton. The same Interlagos circuit had produced a one-point title swing before; we covered it in our look at Hamilton’s last-corner pass on Glock in 2008 and in Räikkönen’s one-point title in 2007 . item.title: El Paso boxer Nayeli Rodriguez earns win vs. Nat Dove on MVP card
item.description: El Paso boxer Nayeli Rodriguez earned arguably her best professional win via split decision against unbeaten Nat Dove in a super flyweight matchup. The win over Dove on Sunday, Nov. 8, on a Most Valuable Promotions card in Arlington, avenged a draw from their first fight in May 2025. The eight-round fight was hotly contested, with Rodriguez winning 77-75 on two judges' scorecards and Dove winning 77-75 on the other judges' scorecards. Dove succeeded with a sharp jab and consistent body work , while Rodriguez found success with head-and-body combinations in the later rounds. Rodriguez improves to 8-2-1 and Dove is now 8-1-1. "I was able to get a good tempo going and with both of us having fought each other, I had an idea of what she was going to," Rodriguez said. "The second fight between us was better and really intense." Rodriguez rebounded from a 10-round decision loss to Katherine Lindenmuth in El Paso on July 16. "I'm not a quitter and that loss this past summer motivated to come back and be even stronger," Rodriguez said. Felix F. FC Köln. Having been criticised for failing to live up to expectations since his €35 million move from PSV in the summer of 2025, the 24-year-old United States international was handed a rare start and impressed head coach Carles Martínez. item.title: Open Championship returning to Carnoustie in 2029 for first time in 11 years
item.description: The Open Championship is returning to Carnoustie in 2029. The R&A announced Monday that the 157th edition of the oldest major championship in the world would return to Carnoustie for the ninth time. The last Open held at the venue was 2018, when Francesco Molinari held off Tiger Woods and others for his lone major title. Other winners at Carnoustie include Tommy Armour, Sir Henry Cotton, Ben Hogan, Gary Player, Tom Watson, Paul Lawrie and Padraig Harrington. “Carnoustie is a world-class championship venue where some of golf’s greatest players have lifted the Claret Jug and the return of The Open to these famous links after more than a decade will give fans the opportunity to be part of another memorable chapter in the Championship’s history," R&A executive chief Mark Darbon said. “We want to continue to deliver an outstanding experience for players, fans and our partners at one of the world’s great sporting events and so have worked closely in collaboration with Carnoustie to help ensure their plans to enhance the venue also support successful stagings of The Open in the years ahead. “We are grateful to Carnoustie’s ownership and management, the Scottish Government and local authorities for their support in bringing The Open back to Angus and look forward to another memorable Championship in 2029.” The 157th Open Championship is set for July 19-22, 2029. The Open will head to St. Andrews in 2027 before going to Royal Lytham and St. Annes in August 2028, moving back a month to accommodate the Olympic Games in Los Angeles. Ryan Fox won the 2026 Open at Royal Birkdale. Cameron Jourdan is an assistant editor of Golfweek, covering college and amateur golf, the PGA Tour and plenty more. item.title: Michael Carrick is ‘clear’ about his plans as he clings onto Man Utd job
item.description: Michael Carrick remains confident in his ability to oversee Manchester United’s resurgence after a “right mixed” three weeks left his team in the relegation zone and the head coach’s future under scrutiny. The 20-time league champions will spend the November international break in 18th place as their wait to add to August’s solitary Premier League win against Ipswich continued against Aston Villa . Carrick insisted afterwards that he would not walk away from a job that looked like it could be taken from him a fortnight ago and the international break provides an opportunity for the club to take stock. As the team continued to receive more and more positive updates on Campbell’s condition, the focus shifted back to football and preparing for a gritty Miami Dolphins team. The rallying cry for the week was to prepare and play as Jack Campbell would—with ruthless devotion and an unstoppable work ethic. item.title: Ajsa Sivka drawing Elena Delle Donne comparisons is a terrifying warning to the SEC
item.description: Kentucky women’s basketball head coach Kenny Brooks already called Ajsa Sivka his best passer, but after Sunday’s shootout against No. 25 NC State, the first-year wing from Slovenia proved she might just be the best overall player on the Kentucky roster. Sivka completely took over the game against the Wolfpack. She exploded for 32 points and tied a program record with eight 3-pointers. She got to the rim at will, threaded brilliant passes through the defense, and officially broke onto the national scene, with television announcers comparing her to college basketball legend Elena Delle Donne. For fans who follow international basketball, this breakout performance was not a surprise. The 6-foot-4 guard was selected 10th overall by the Chicago Sky in the 2025 WNBA Draft, but she opted to remain in Europe to represent Slovenia in the FIBA Women’s European Basketball Championship. During that tournament run, she shot 50 percent from the floor, highlighted by a flawless 4-of-4 performance from deep against Italy. That elite efficiency earned her MVP honors at the 2023 FIBA U18 European Championship. But the comparison is what excites me. For those unfamiliar with the women’s game, Delle Donne is an absolute legend. During her historic career at Delaware, Delle Donne was the ultimate mismatch. She was a towering perimeter player who could handle the ball, shoot from anywhere, and score at will. She led the entire nation in scoring as a junior with 28.1 points per game and once dropped 54 points in a single contest. Delle Donne was a dominant force who carried her team deep into the NCAA Tournament, combining elite frontcourt size with traditional guard skills and scoring over half of Delaware’s points, finishing with 33 in a loss to No. 2 seed Kentucky, 69-62, in 2013. Overall, Sivka was 11-for-17 from the floor and 8-for-12 from deep. She also added 5 rebounds and 3 assists, though several of her passes didn’t count as assists because of missed shots. 6'4" @KentuckyWBB guard Ajsa Sivka was a problem for NC State 😳 She was selected No. 10 overall in the 2025 WNBA draft 😯 32 PTS 11-17 FG 8-12 3-PT FG pic.twitter.com/X32kaw4sJi — SEC Network (@SECNetwork) November 8, 2026 If Sivka can replicate anything close to that Delle Donne impact, Kentucky will be a massive problem for opponents all year long.

item.title: Rangers Daily: Korpisalo ‘going to get better;’ Devils Hellebuyck decision
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Joonas Koripsalo is a pretty low-key guy. So, it wasn’t a big surprise that the veteran goalie was pretty matter of fact when discussing his first start and win for the New York Rangers on Saturday night in Seattle. “I felt OK, there’s still some stuff to clean up, and it’s obviously going to get better as we go along,” Korpisalo said postgame , after the Rangers skated to a 4-3 victory over the Kraken . He’s right, of course. There’s stuff to clean up and it should get better moving forward — for him and the team. The Rangers led 4-0 before surrendering three third-period goals to sweat out, what turned out to be, their third consecutive victory. Korpisalo made 25 saves in his Rangers debut — one that was delayed by more than a month after a foot infection sidelined him after he backed up Igor Shesterkin on opening night against his former team, the Boston Bruins. You know the rest of the story. Shesterkin sustained a season-ending knee injury, rookie Dylan Garand — fresh off clearing waivers — played 12 games in a row (10 starts, two in relief), and Rangers nation eagerly awaited Korpisalo’s return. The irony there is rich, of course, considering most fans didn’t want the 32-year-old goalie in the first place, when the Rangers traded for him this past summer. Garand was the chosen one to be No. 2 behind Shesterkin on Broadway. But now, everyone realized Garand needs a proven NHL partner to share the goaltending load with Shesterkin done for the season. “You know what it takes, right? So, all that time I was working out, making sure I’m as ready as possible to go when it’s my time to play,” Korpisalo said about knowing how to prepare himself as a veteran when he was sidelined. This isn’t the return of Shesterkin, perhaps the best goalie in the sport. But Korpisalo’s return is important to the Rangers because it brings balance to the goaltending position, gives the team two viable options to play each night, and should bring out the best in a more rested Garand. item.description: OBETZ − Some legends take years to build; others spend four years cementing their status in stone. Estadt led a powerhouse local group of four total All-Ohio recipients by shattering her own school record with a blistering time of 18:14.5 to capture third place overall in the girls Division IV race, capping a decorated career with her third state podium finish in four years. Setting a new standard for the Colts Estadt wasn't the only local runner rewriting record books on the OHSAA big stage. Meadowbrook sophomore Vincent Campbell delivered an strong performance in the boys Division III action, recording a time of 15:10.9 to place fifth overall. Shenandoah runners shine on the big stage Back in Division IV, Shenandoah added a second All-Ohio honoree as sophomore Joel Tewksbary powered his way to a 20th-place finish with a time of 16:19.1. Paced by Tewksbary's efforts, the Shenandoah boys team put together a gritty team performance to take 17th overall in a heavily contested Division IV field of 24 teams. However, Woolen himself does not want to leave the Eagles, per a post on X by Eliot Shorr-Parks. The Super Bowl LX champion claimed that while the final decision rests with the front office and his agent, he himself does not want to leave. Tariq Woolen says his preference is to stay in Philadelphia with the Eagles pic.twitter.com/TZlDGECRUe Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Eliot Shorr-Parks (@EliotShorrParks) November 8, 2026 “Oh most definitely, I mean, if you woke up everyday with your friends, some of your close friends and you’all worked hard as hell everyday and you just up and disappeared when shit got hard, then it would seem kind of weird especially when it’s on you, you know?” he said. “If it’s up to how we in the gym and my agent, then I am going to leave it to them. But knowing me as a person I have worked hard with these guys and I would love to be here and stay here with them.” Woolen has recorded 30 tackles, one forced fumble and six passes defended through eight games. The former fifth-round pick in 2022 earned Pro Bowl recognition as a rookie in 2022 and finished the 2025 season with 41 tackles, one interception and 12 passes defended. His size and speed mean that he is likely to have no dearth of interested teams, with a range of outfits, including the Buffalo Bills and the Detroit Lions. Philadelphia have slumped to seven consecutive defeats after the latest loss against the New York Giants. Jalen Hurts is reportedly out for the season, which has only intensified the rumors as Philadelphia seem intent on giving up contracts that can give them immediate value. item.title: Jacksonville Jaguars to trade for Atlanta Falcons safety Jessie Bates III
item.description: Safety Jessie Bates III (L) started all 17 games in each of his last three full seasons with the Atlanta Falcons. File Photo by AJ Sisco/UPI Nov. 9 (UPI) -- The Jacksonville Jaguars agreed to acquire Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates III through a trade with the Atlanta Falcons, a league source told UPI on Monday. Bates, 29, is on the final year of his contract. The nine-year veteran totaled 60 combined tackles, four passes defensed, three forced fumbles, an interception and a fumble return for a touchdown through nine starts this season. He would join a Jaguars secondary that includes Antonio Johnson at free safety and cornerbacks Travis Hunter, Montaric Brown and Jourdan Lewis. DeMarcco Hellams and Sydney Brown are now candidates for more snaps at strong safety for the Falcons, next to starting free safety Xavier Watts. The Jaguars have the third-best defense in the AFC in terms of yards allowed per game. They allowed the second-fewest rushing yards per game among AFC teams, trailing only the Pittsburgh Steelers. The Jaguars' pass defense allowed the eighth-most yards per game among AFC teams. The Jaguars (6-2) will take on the Tennessee Titans (1-7) at 1 p.m. EST Sunday in Nashville. The Falcons (3-6) will host the Kansas City Chiefs (6-2) at 1 p.m. Sunday in Atlanta.

item.title: ‘Don’t know…’ – Austin Reaves comments on his courtside interaction with a Detroit Pistons fan
item.description: Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images Austin Reaves was seen closely having conversation with a fan seated courtside during the Los Angeles Lakers’ game against the Detroit Pistons. With the Lakers holding a 60-45 lead in the second quarter, Reaves approached the fan to have a conversation with him. The others seated next to the fan were visibly smiling as Reaves spoke to him. It was definitely not a pleasant conversation, as he waved goodbye to the fan when he hit the dagger to help the Lakers win the game. The Lakers lined up without Luka Doncic, and all the responsibility was naturally on Austin Reaves. He seemed to relish the opportunity, as he scored 43 points to lead the Purple and Gold to a 121-116 win. In typical Luka style, Reaves reminded the fan seated on the courtside of who he was and replied to the trash talk by putting up a monstrous performance. “I don’t know what you’re talking about,” replied Reaves when asked about the courtside interaction. Reaves was outstanding and did his best to help the Lakers extend their winning streak to five games. Playing against a tough defensive unit, with the likes of Ausar Thompson and Ron Holland, Reaves showed the world that he has what it takes to lead without Doncic. The 28-year-old had some big performances last season as well, when both Doncic and LeBron James were out. “Luka is an incredible player, and I think there are times when he’s playing that A.R. kind of has to take a secondary role,” Lakers centre Walker Kessler told reporters after the game. “But you could see tonight that he’s a very capable player.” The Lakers are now 2-0 without Doncic in the lineup. Reaves is averaging 29.5 points and attempting 21.5 shots in the absence of Doncic. Both of these stats show that Reaves can definitely lead the way for the Lakers if the Slovenian has any setbacks, which obviously is not something the team would ever want, as he is in fiery form this season.
